name: Neropalin Blue
lede: Neropalin Blue is a light, muted blue from Ridgway's 1912 atlas, under a name that appears in no other source our library consulted.

sections.title: A Ridgway coinage with no other trace
sections.body:
Ridgway's atlas places this value at plate XXII, hue 49 (starred, meaning an intermediate hue not on the main wheel), tone b, first recorded in 1912 [1]. Unlike most of his plate names, our library finds no later dictionary, standard or web source repeating *Neropalin*, so its coinage and meaning are undocumented beyond the plate itself [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 classifies the hue as a light purplish blue, about 4.7 units from that block's reference chip [2].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[cornflower|Cornflower]], and it sits close to [[berlin-blue|Berlin Blue]], [[periwinkle|Periwinkle]] and the darker, named [[newport|Newport]] on the same blue stretch of the chart [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a color within six units of Neropalin Blue covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 127 works, about one in two hundred, as photographed [3]. Johan Thomas Lundbye carries it in 4 of his 38 archived paintings, far above his average, and it is strongest in paintings from Norway and Denmark, peaking in the 1900s decade [3]. Its most common company on canvas is Cornflower and Periwinkle, both close in hue [3]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished canvases read as screen colors, not pigment tests [3].
